title: Upgrade Node.js for Next.js 16
steps: Use Node.js 20.9.0 or later for Next.js 16.
statement: The Next.js 16 upgrade guide sets Node.js 20.9.0 as the minimum; this migration step is satisfied by a declared Node.js version at or above that threshold.
sourceEvidence: The guide's runtime support table sets Node.js minimum version to 20.9.0.

title: Rename middleware to proxy
steps: Rename middleware.ts or middleware.js to proxy.ts or proxy.js.
Rename the named export middleware to proxy.
Review runtime use: proxy uses Node.js runtime; Edge runtime is not supported in proxy.
statement: The Next.js 16 upgrade guide documents renaming middleware files and exports to proxy and states that Edge runtime is not supported in proxy.
sourceEvidence: Section “middleware to proxy” contains the two rename instructions and states proxy runtime is nodejs and cannot be configured; edge is not supported.

title: Review PPR configuration for Next.js 16
steps: Remove the experimental_ppr route segment option.
Review the official Cache Components migration guidance before enabling the new configuration.
statement: The Next.js 16 upgrade guide says experimental PPR flags/configuration were removed and directs users to Cache Components migration patterns; it advises users of PPR in Next.js 15 canaries to stay on that canary pending migration guidance.
sourceEvidence: PPR section states experimental_ppr is removed; Next 15 Canary PPR differs, and users on it should stay on their current canary; Cache Components migration patterns are linked.

title: Migrate to asynchronous request APIs
steps: Await params and searchParams where documented.
Use the provided codemod or documented temporary synchronous compatibility access where required.
statement: The Next.js 15 upgrade guide documents the APIs becoming asynchronous and provides codemod and temporary synchronous access guidance.
sourceEvidence: Async API section shows before/after examples such as `await cookies()` and describes a codemod and temporary synchronous compatibility casts.
